findings.what: The S1 deny and allow-1433 checks scan all of network.bicep. If the private-endpoint NSG's deny-all is deleted, the checker still passes on the app NSG's deny-all
findings.why: This is the same weakness A2 R3 found in I5. The deny regex at lines 179-180 and the 1433/Allow checks at lines 177-178 aren't tied to the NSG on snet-private-endpoints. Take the mutant with the deny-all-inbound rule removed from privateEndpointNsg. Default AllowVnetInBound would then let the whole VNet and any peered network reach 1433, which is exactly the S1 exposure. The checker still passes because appIntegrationNsg matches 'direction Inbound ... access Deny'. The message 'the SQL NSG must deny all other inbound traffic' claims more than the check proves. The infrastructure at HEAD is correct. The gap is in the oracle. gate.pipeline-schema@c4032df names a mutant for R3 only, none for S1.

findings.rule_id: code-quality: comments must be true and explainable
findings.what: 'The agent's network also needs to be allowed by the pool' is unclear and out of date. Since S1, the agents must fall inside agentAddressPrefix (the NSG allow) and be peered
findings.why: A pool doesn't allow networks. After c4032df the real requirement is that the agents' range is in the 1433 allow rule (agentAddressPrefix, network.bicep) and that their network is peered to or inside the VNet. The pool comment at lines 21-24 doesn't mention the NSG range either. An agent outside agentAddressPrefix fails the migrations step. That fails closed, but the template sends the operator in the wrong direction. Code-quality rule: a comment explains the why, and it must be true.

findings.rule_id: F5-acceptance: no secrets / config by environment
findings.what: agentAddressPrefix is a committed placeholder (10.30.0.0/24, the same in all 3 envs). The comment says 'not committed', but the pipeline has no override, so a commit is the only way to set it
findings.why: sqlAdminGroupObjectId has a placeholder plus a variable-group override (--parameters sqlAdminGroupObjectId=$(sqlAdminGroupObjectId)). agentAddressPrefix has no such path, so 'the real address range ... is not committed. Set it before the first deployment' can only be done by committing it. An address range isn't a secret, so committing it is fine. But the comment and the mechanism contradict each other, and David will be asked which one is intended. The same text appears in test.bicepparam and prod.bicepparam, line 10.

A2 S1: RESOLVED in the infrastructure. Both subnets have an NSG. The private-endpoint subnet sets privateEndpointNetworkPolicies 'Enabled', so the NSG applies to the endpoint. The SQL NSG allows TCP 1433 from appIntegrationPrefix and agentAddressPrefix to the endpoint subnet at priority 100, and denies all other inbound at 4000, ahead of the default AllowVnetInBound. The integration subnet denies all inbound, which is fine because App Service integration is outbound only and NSGs are stateful. Peering keeps the agents' source IPs, so the allow rule works across a peer. See R1 for the strength of the matching oracle.
